title: Pseudo-classes and Pseudo-elements
description: Using pseudo-classes and pseudo-elements to style elements based on state or structure without adding extra HTML.

flashcards.question: What is a pseudo-class in CSS?
flashcards.answer: A keyword added to selectors that specifies a special state of the element, like :hover or :focus.

flashcards.question: Give an example of a commonly used pseudo-class.
What is a pseudo-element in CSS?
flashcards.answer: A keyword added to selectors to style a specific part of an element, like ::before or ::after.

flashcards.question: How do you denote a pseudo-element in CSS?
flashcards.answer: Using double colons (::) before the pseudo-element name.

flashcards.question: What does the ::before pseudo-element do?
flashcards.answer: Inserts content before the content of an element.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between :hover and ::before?
flashcards.answer: :hover is a pseudo-class targeting element state, ::before is a pseudo-element targeting part of element content.

flashcards.question: Can pseudo-classes be chained with other selectors?
flashcards.answer: Yes, for example a:hover or li:nth-child(2).

flashcards.question: What does the :nth-child() pseudo-class do?
flashcards.answer: Selects elements based on their position among siblings.

flashcards.question: Is it possible to style the first letter of a paragraph using CSS?
Are pseudo-elements part of the DOM?
flashcards.answer: No, pseudo-elements are not part of the DOM; they are abstractions to style parts of elements.
